## Remediation {#remediation}

1. Stop using the affected package version immediately.
2. Clean systems where one of these packages has been installed. See StepSecurity's [Mini Shai-Hulud recovery steps](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem#for-the-community-recovery-steps).
3. Rotate all secrets accessible from those systems.
4. Check cloud audit logs for suspicious activity.
5. Monitor connections to the following command and control indicators:
    - `api[.]masscan[.]cloud`
    - `filev2[.]getsession[.]org`
    - `git-tanstack[.]com`
    - `seed1[.]getsession[.]org`
    - `83[.]142[.]209[.]194` (PyPI payload host)

content.text:
The affected SDK package versions are:

- **npm**
  - `@mistralai/mistralai`: `2.2.2`, `2.2.3`, `2.2.4`
  - `@mistralai/mistralai-azure`: `1.7.1`, `1.7.2`, `1.7.3`
  - `@mistralai/mistralai-gcp`: `1.7.1`, `1.7.2`, `1.7.3`

- **PyPI**
  - `mistralai`: `2.4.6`

[Affected versions](https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/security-advisories/MAI-2026-002#affected-versions)

If you installed one of these versions, you should:
1. Stop using the affected package version immediately.
2. Clean systems where any of these packages were installed (see StepSecurity's recovery steps).
3. Rotate all secrets accessible from those systems.
4. Check cloud audit logs for suspicious activity.
5. Monitor connections to the listed command and control indicators.

[Remediation](https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/security-advisories/MAI-2026-002#remediation)
